entries.headline: Kyiv strike casualty report relayed
entries.summary: War Watch Intel relayed a Suspilne report quoting Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko that two people were killed in a Russian strike in the city’s Obolon district. The visible quotation is truncated, so no further incident details are stated here; this remains an attributed publisher report.

entries.headline: Elevated radio activity and U.S. aircraft reported
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported coded U.S. Air Force radio broadcasts at nearly four times normal across global hotspots, alongside transport aircraft and a nuclear command aircraft over the United States. The post supplies no baseline or detailed locations for that comparison; these remain publisher claims.

entries.headline: Priority Air Transport activity questioned
entries.summary: War Watch Intel noted numerous Priority Air Transport aircraft airborne and asked whether the activity was normal. The post did not establish a baseline, aircraft count or mission, so it does not confirm unusual activity.

entries.headline: U.S. aircraft activity and fifteen radio broadcasts reported
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported multiple U.S. Air Force surveillance and transport aircraft airborne over the United States, together with a nuclear command aircraft. It said fifteen coded radio broadcasts had been heard that day; the post did not establish the missions of those aircraft.

entries.headline: IDF weapons-shipment strike claim relayed
entries.summary: War Watch Intel relayed an IDF statement claiming a strike on a weapons shipment moving from Syria to Lebanon and intended for Hezbollah. The quoted statement is truncated; further strike details are not established by the visible post.

entries.headline: Normal-level aircraft and radio activity reported
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported U.S. Air Force transport aircraft and a NATO surveillance aircraft airborne across the North Sea and elsewhere, with eleven coded radio broadcasts heard that day. It described activity as normal.

entries.headline: Crimean Bridge traffic-halt report relayed
entries.summary: War Watch Intel relayed an Al Jazeera Arabic report citing Interfax that traffic had halted on the Crimean Bridge. The quoted text is truncated after a reference to Ukrainian targeting, so the post does not establish further attack details here.

entries.headline: E-6B route question posted
entries.summary: War Watch Intel asked whether an E-6B was crossing the Atlantic or heading offshore. The post posed a question; it did not confirm a route, destination or mission.

entries.headline: Hourly radio and aircraft activity reported
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported four coded U.S. Air Force radio broadcasts in the past hour and two nuclear command-and-control jets airborne over the continental United States alongside transport aircraft. The visible post is truncated after “spy…”, so no further aircraft detail is stated.

entries.headline: Commercial-shipping and Romanian warning claim posted
entries.summary: War Watch Intel claimed commercial vessels were being struck in NATO territorial waters and Romania was issuing navigation warnings. The post is truncated before specifying the area to avoid; locations, incidents and warning details are not independently verified here.

entries.headline: Transport activity near Korea and Japan reported
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported U.S. military transport aircraft airborne over the continental United States, activity near Korea and Japan at nearly four times normal, and one coded U.S. Air Force radio broadcast heard that hour.

entries.headline: Six U.S. Air Force transport aircraft reported
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported six U.S. Air Force transport aircraft airborne over the United States and described activity as slightly above normal after recent civilian aviation disruptions.

skyglass.caption: Military aircraft movement reports.

entries.headline: Aircraft departures after FAA ground stop examined
entries.summary: SkyGlass introduced a thread showing some jets it observed departing after the previous day's FAA ground stop began.

entries.headline: FAA ground-stop aircraft counts reported
entries.summary: SkyGlass reported 7,373 aircraft airborne over the continental United States before the previous day's FAA ground stop, with a low of 424 reached 21 minutes after it lifted. It reported general aviation represented 36% and airlines 26% of aircraft still airborne.

entries.headline: Three-dimensional airspace advisories demonstrated
entries.summary: SkyGlass described its Overwatch display of SIGMETs, AIRMETs and temporary flight restrictions in three dimensions, from their lower to upper altitude limits, using NOAA and FAA data.

entries.headline: Business-jet analysis using SkyGlass MCP demonstrated
entries.summary: SkyGlass demonstrated querying business-jet activity from August through October through its MCP service, using AVIAR Labs data.

entries.headline: NASA806 U-2 movement reported
entries.summary: SkyGlass reported NASA806, described as a U-2, at about 60,000 feet and heading eastward.

entries.headline: Business-jet activity and growth leaders reported
entries.summary: SkyGlass reported that over the 13 weeks to 1 November, the Phenom 300 accounted for 9.4% of tracked business-jet activity, the Latitude 7.1% and the XLS 6.1%. Among aircraft types with at least a 1% share, it said the G650 grew 17.3% and the Falcon 2000 grew 15.8% when comparing the latest four weeks with the first four, while activity across all types rose 8.0%.

entries.headline: SCORE90 Global Hawk sighting reported
entries.summary: SkyGlass reported tracking SCORE90, a Northrop Grumman Global Hawk (Q4), off the Mid-Atlantic coast. It said the aircraft was spotted at about 49,900 feet at 2:44 p.m. ET on 3 November and last seen around 3:01 p.m. about nine miles east-southeast of Ocean City, Maryland.

entries.headline: NTSB weather focus in Sunday crash relayed
entries.summary: SkyGlass relayed comments from its founder about air-traffic-control audio from Sunday's crash and said the audio would not be shared out of respect. It reported that the NTSB was focusing on weather and offered condolences to those affected.

entries.headline: NetJets and Flexjet activity growth reported
entries.summary: SkyGlass reported tracked NetJets and Flexjet activity up 11.0% in October 2026 from October 2025, while full-service Jet A rose from $7.50 to $7.86. It said fractional flying did not slow and that the figures were pulled with the SkyGlass MCP.

entries.headline: N722BD Learjet 60 crash reported
entries.summary: SkyGlass reported that Learjet 60 N722BD, flying from Austin to North Eleuthera, crashed near Military Trail in Palm Beach County on Sunday afternoon, killing all nine people aboard. It said the NTSB was investigating and shared an AVIAR Labs Overwatch replay.

entries.headline: Signature Access FBO pricing changes examined
entries.summary: SkyGlass said Signature Access prices core fixed-base-operator access by aircraft size, ramp time and location, while limiting event fees from 2027. It argued that ramp dwell time and demand are operational variables FBOs should track, citing RampWatch as a way to show them.

entries.headline: BACE2026 four-field business-jet total revisited
entries.summary: SkyGlass reported that 1,040 distinct business jets moved through four Las Vegas fields during BACE2026 show week. It said the RampWatch board prompted conversations, including direct-message feedback that ramp personnel wanted views of their own traffic, and linked to a replay.
